item.title: OpenAI takes on Microsoft with the launch of what feels a whole lot like ChatGPT’s own office suite
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: OpenAI's newly announced suite of office features puts it into mor direct competition with more traditional software companies.

item.title: Dutch police arrest ShinyHunters hacker accused of planning two murders
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: Dutch police said the hacker, arrested for being part of the ShinyHunters cybercriminal gang, had plans to organize the murder of two people on his laptop.

item.title: AI-powered app maker Wabi pivots to a messaging experience
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Wabi is repositioning its prompt-based app builder as a personal AI agent that can create interfaces on demand, combining chat, apps and ongoing tasks.

item.title: OpenAI launches Dots, its bubbly agentic avatar
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: Dots are meant to operate independent of any specific hardware or interface, pursuing user-defined goals continuously in the background with minimal oversight.

item.title: OpenAI gives Codex reusable cloud environments that work across devices
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: OpenAI is expanding Codex with reusable cloud development environments, a revamped CLI with voice controls, new code review tools and a security-focused product for scanning repositories and preparing fixes.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Sol, says it nearly matches GPT-6 Astra and costs less
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: OpenAI says GPT-6.1 Sol delivers significant improvements over GPT-6 Sol across complex professional tasks, including code writing and debugging, document understanding, and executing multi-step business workflows.

item.title: OpenAI expands ChatGPT’s plugins with app-like interfaces and automations
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: OpenAI is expanding ChatGPT plugins with dedicated sidebar homes, interactive panels, file viewers, improved discovery, and support for automations.

item.title: Can a chatbot fix the government maze? The White House is about to find out
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silberling
item.description: America.gov is intended to simplify the process of navigating government bureaucracy, but language models are imperfect and remain prone to hallucinations, which could cause new issues.

item.title: Instinct founder said more than 50% of transactions on the platform are travel-related
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Instinct founder said the platform is growing 10% day by day, with transaction volume increasing at a similar rate.

item.title: After losing his voice to cancer, this founder is building ‘glasses for voice’
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: Uhura Bionics, part of the Startup Battlefield 200 at TechCrunch Disrupt, wants to replace flat, robotics voice devices with one that carries emotions.

item.title: Oura shelves its $2.2B IPO, citing ‘uncertainty’ in the market
item.dc:creator: Ram Iyer
item.description: The postponement of the IPO will delay some of the company's plans for its proceeds from the IPO, as well as those of its shareholders.

item.title: With Dazzle, Marissa Mayer bets your camera roll has more info on your life than your inbox
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: Mayer argues that if a photo is worth a thousand words, your camera roll is worth millions. By analyzing all the photos stored on your phone, Dazzle claims to understand your hobbies, interests, food, and style preferences, how you like to spend their time, and with whom.

item.title: Meta is expanding its AI agent Muse to small businesses
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: The tech giant says the agent can help owners run their business and find new customers.

item.title: Still running iOS 26? Update your iPhones, iPads, and Macs for this urgent security fix
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: Apple says the bug was used to attack "specific targeted individuals" running iOS 26, which the majority of Apple customers are still using.

item.title: Fireflies adds dictation to its desktop notetaking apps
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Fireflies said that it won't charge extra for the new dictation feature, which can be used with any desktop app.

item.title: OpenAI apologizes to Australia after its AI agents breached government sites
item.dc:creator: Kate Park
item.description: The company also detailed how some of those breaches had happened, and outlined additional measures it is taking to assess the impact of the events.

item.title: Reco raises $55M as AI agent security startups crowd the market
item.dc:creator: Ram Iyer
item.description: The round builds on a $30 million fundraise in February, taking the company's total funding to $140 million.

item.title: Protego Ventures closes debut $125 million fund for Israeli defense tech
item.dc:creator: Anna Heim
item.description: Protego Ventures, the first and largest dedicated defense tech VC in Israel, just completed its final $125 million closing, TechCrunch learned exclusively.

item.title: Ex-Tesla team raises $12.5M to put supply chains on autopilot
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: Atomic's agentic supply chain software is now being used by companies like DoorDash and HelloFresh.

item.title: Anthropic’s prospectus details losses, growth, and, yes, a warning that its AI could end humanity
item.dc:creator: Connie Loizos
item.description: In its prospectus, Anthropic just told investors it's losing tens of billions of dollars a year, but also growing like crazy, and — oh yeah — its own AI might pose an existential risk to humanity.
